claim: On systemd hosts the session bus is managed by the user's service manager and is ALWAYS the same socket across all logins/TTYs/desktops: DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/run/user/1000/bus — logind shares the session across virtual terminals
stance_target: an agent on a systemd (NixOS) host can rely on the stable user-bus socket path /run/user/<uid>/bus
scope_conditions: systemd hosts with user services (NixOS included); Chimera with dinit user services behaves the same
quoted_support: When using Systemd ... the logind daemon tracking the session and the session is shared for all logins regardless of virtual terminal. And Systemd also manages the session bus for you, thanks to user services, so regardless of the virtual console or X11 or Wayland desktop or whatever you go to, you will always get the same session bus socket, and it will look like this: DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/run/user/1000/bus

claim: On non-systemd distros without user services, the session bus is launched per-session (dbus-launch / dbus-run-session / desktop environment) producing an abstract socket like unix:abstract=/tmp/dbus-... that is invisible to other sessions (e.g. other TTYs)
stance_target: per-session bus sockets are the failure mode a fleet agent must not depend on; only the user-bus convention gives a stable address
quoted_support: In a usual non-systemd distro, the D-Bus session bus is launched either explicitly (using dbus-launch or dbus-run-session depending on context), or by the desktop environment. That means things using the session bus for example within an X11 instance will see the bus, but if you switch tty and log in, nothing in that tty will be able to.

claim: You must NEVER run anything with dbus-run-session (or similar) on a system that already has a global/user-manager session bus: it launches a NESTED session bus whose processes are invisible to the global bus, and it is unnecessary
stance_target: an agent must never self-launch a session bus on NixOS; it should connect to /run/user/<uid>/bus
scope_conditions: any host with an existing user-manager bus (systemd hosts, Chimera)
quoted_support: Additionally, you should never run anything with dbus-run-session or similar. Doing so results in a nested session bus being launched which will result in things running in it not being seen by things running in the global session bus. It's also completely unnecessary.

claim: Chimera Linux achieves the same out-of-box user-bus behaviour as systemd via dinit user services plus dbus-dinit-links default service links for both system and session bus, showing the user-bus-at-/run/user/<uid>/bus pattern is service-manager-generic, not systemd-specific
stance_target: portability of the user-bus pattern across service managers (relevant if jupiterOS mixes init systems)
scope_conditions: Chimera Linux with dinit and the dbus package
quoted_support: Since Chimera comes with implicit support for user services, it can also afford to handle this. When you install the dbus package in Chimera, you will typically get the -dinit subpackage with the service files, as well as -dinit-links which contains default service links for both the system and session bus.
